options: Energy that is stored up and waiting
Energy a moving object already has
Sound produced by a jinking plank
questions.explanation: Potential energy is stored — it waits until it can act, unlike the kinetic energy a moving object carries.
questions.misconception: Groups motion energy (kinetic) with stored energy; position, not motion, is what stores it.

questions.prompt: A 4 kg block sits on a 5 m shelf (g = 10 N/kg). What is its gravitational potential energy?
questions.misconception: Leaving out g (4 × 5 = 20) or squaring wrongly (400) are common slips; mass × g × height is the full recipe.

questions.prompt: You double the height of a shelf holding a box. What happens to its potential energy?
questions.explanation: Height appears once in PE = mgh, so double the height → double the stored energy.
questions.misconception: The squared-habit from kinetic energy slips in; potential energy is linear in height.

questions.prompt: When the block is released from the shelf, where does its potential energy go?
options: It turns into kinetic energy of the falling block
It stays stored inside the same height
questions.explanation: The stored energy converts to kinetic energy as the block accelerates — energy changes form, never vanishes.
questions.misconception: Treating loss as destruction; energy is conserved and simply shifts into motion.

questions.prompt: In what unit do we measure potential energy?
questions.explanation: All energy is measured in joules; newtons measure force, meters measure length.
questions.misconception: Mixing the energy unit with force (N) or the height unit (m) is a classic slip.
